slides.title: Validate on the way in, encode on the way out
slides.summary: Validation rejects bad data, sanitization cleans it, and encoding makes it safe where it's shown.
body: Three different jobs that are often confused:

ul: Validation checks input matches what you expect (type, length, format, range) and rejects it otherwise.
Sanitization removes or rewrites dangerous parts, e.g. stripping <script> from rich text.
Encoding converts data so it's inert in its output context: HTML, URL, SQL parameter.

body: <mark>Frontend validation is for user experience. The server must validate again, because attackers skip your UI.</mark>

body.note: Prefer allowlists (what's permitted) to blocklists (what's forbidden). Attackers are better at finding what you forgot to block.

items.label: Output
items.sub: Encode for the context it's shown in

figure.alt: Data flows left to right through four stages. Browser: an untrusted zone where validation gives fast feedback but can be skipped. The API at the trust boundary validates again against a schema, the authoritative check, rejecting a value like an email of 5,000 characters. Storage uses parameterised queries so input is never part of the SQL text. Output encodes the value for its context, HTML, attribute or URL, so a stored name like <script> is shown as text. A dashed line marks the trust boundary between the browser and the API.

slides.title: Validating in practice
slides.summary: Share one schema between client and server, and validate everything that crosses a trust boundary.

ul: Share a schema (Zod, Valibot, JSON Schema) between frontend and backend so the rules can't drift.
Validate all inputs, not just form fields: URL parameters, postMessage data, localStorage, and API responses.
Constrain URLs by parsing them with new URL() and checking the protocol and host.
Limit sizes of text and files, and check file types by their content on the server, not by extension.

body: <mark>Parse, don't just check: turn unknown input into a typed value once, at the boundary, and use only that value afterwards.</mark>
